params.body:
Signups moved to the site with the move to Laravel (`AuthController::register`, `ClayLeads.php` in gentells-site). The pipeline kept its own:

- **`POST /auth/register`** is public (the `/auth/*` routes are handled before the staff gate), and the Observatory's basic auth does not cover `/api/pipeline`: an empty POST from outside answers 400 "Missing email, password, or name". Anyone could create reader accounts in the pipeline's `users` table, and each one went to Clay as a `trial_signup` lead. No client calls it: not the site, the dashboard or the Studio. The two reader accounts in the table are from before 13 August.
- **`clay.mjs`**, whose only caller was that route, and its backfill (the site has its own, `gentells:clay-backfill`).

Both go, with the Clay setting blanked in the auto-deploy test run and the paragraph in `CLAUDE.md`, which now points to the site.

The gating test gains a check that every route on its pre-gate list exists, so the list cannot keep a door that is gone. It found two more stale entries, now corrected:
- `/api/elixir`: the server's path is `/elixir`; nginx adds the prefix.
- `/auth/logout`: no such route.

Stray comments announcing routes that went with the React site (`/trends/public`, `/articles/published`) are removed, and a `POST /chat` comment moves back above its route.

Tests: 953 pass (the Clay tests went with the file). Lint: 0 undefined names, unused unchanged.

Checked and clean, so not in this PR:
- every route the Studio calls exists;
- every pipeline route has a caller, apart from the curation mail links and Elixir's health reads, which live outside the repos;
- gentells.com has no class, view, command or package that nothing uses.
params.title: Signups are the site's: the pipeline's public register route and clay.mjs go
